description: One membership-changing transition — add, remove, or reclassify across the canonical member predicate — carrying exactly one same-family/scope horizon successor referencing the current predecessor (ADR-0017 decision 3). The transition is all-or-nothing: a member change without a successor, or a successor without a member change, is malformed and alters nothing. Family and scope are stated once here and bind both halves, so a differently-scoped successor is unrepresentable. A same-member value correction that does not change predicate membership uses the ordinary assertion act and never this kind (ADR-0017 decision 4). Additive over v2: the 'remove' and 'reclassify' member actions may optionally carry 'corresponds_to_fact_id', naming the fact_id of whatever current finding actually took over the withdrawn fact's computational role. This is a bare, checkable claim, not a semantic guarantee — the kernel only records it (packages/kernel/findings.py's FindingState.withdrawal_correspondence) for historical completeness; it never inspects whether the correspondence is 'the same real-world obligation' in any domain's terms, and no migration-adoption check consults it for authority (packages/kernel/findings.py's _refuse_unresolved_nonzero_withdrawals). Omitting the field is still a valid, schema-conformant withdrawal — it simply cannot resolve a 'resolved-required' migration's unresolved predecessor claim on its own.
title: Atomic member transition act payload
